lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Guided practice B: checking and interpreting

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read once, then cover the example and try the guided set from memory.

items.prompt: System: y = x + 2 and y = -x + 6. Does the point (1, 3) satisfy both equations, fail one, or fail both?

steps: Check (1, 3) in the first equation: 1 + 2 = 3, which matches.
Check (1, 3) in the second equation: -1 + 6 = 5, which does not match 3.
The point satisfies the first equation but fails the second, so it fails the second equation only.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Plan A charges a $41 flat fee plus $1 per visit. Plan B charges a $9 flat fee plus $5 per visit. The solution to the system is (8, 49). What does the y-coordinate of the solution represent?
choices: The shared cost, in dollars, when the two plans are equal.
The number of visits after which the two plans cost the same.
The rate Plan B charges per visit.
The difference in cost between the two plans.

items.prompt: System: y = 4x - 8 and y = -x - 3. Which point (x, y) satisfies both equations?
Solve the system: y = 6x + 35 and y = -5x - 31. What is the intersection point (x, y)?
Relationship A: x: 6, 7, 8, 9 y: 20, 16, 12, 8. Relationship B: x: 6, 7, 8, 9 y: 28, 20, 12, 4. At which x-value do the two relationships have the same y-value?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Solve the system: y = -2x + 16 and y = 6x - 48. In which quadrant does the intersection point lie, or does it lie on an axis?

Solve the system:
y = 7x - 26
6x - 4y = 16
Use substitution to find the solution (x, y).

Solve the system:
4x - 9y = 145
4x - 2y = 82
Use elimination to find the solution (x, y).
Classify the system: y = -x - 16 and y = -x + 20. Does it have one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions?
